The Federal Government has adopted a phased and customer-friendly approach to enforcement of
the TIN-bank account linkage policy. The implementation timeline is as follows:

The TIN-bank account linkage policy is a key component of Nigeria's broader fiscal modernization
agenda. When implemented effectively, it will enhance tax compliance, reduce revenue leakage,
and improve the integrity of Nigeria's financial system.

a customer-centric approach by banks and tax authorities. The Federal Government has committed
to a gradual, non-punitive implementation process that prioritizes citizen convenience and

TAX IDENTIFICATION NUMBER (TIN)
BANK ACCOUNT REQUIREMENTS 2026
OFFICIAL GUIDANCE AND CLARIFICATIONS
This document provides comprehensive guidance on the Tax Identification Number (TIN)
requirements for bank account operations beginning January 1, 2026, as mandated under the
Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025. It consolidates official statements from the Nigeria Revenue
Service (NRS), Federal Ministry of Finance, and the Presidential Committee on Fiscal Policy and
Tax Reforms.
Following widespread public concerns and misinformation in December 2025, the Federal
Government issued multiple clarifications to ensure citizens understand the policy, its exemptions,
and practical implementation.
POLICY OVERVIEW
Legal Basis
The requirement for TIN in banking transactions is not entirely new to Nigerian law. It was first
introduced through the Finance Act, 2020, which amended Section 10 of the Personal Income Tax
Act. However, enforcement was inconsistent due to lack of clear regulatory frameworks and limited
institutional capacity.
The Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025 now provides comprehensive legal backing for the
mandatory linkage of TIN to financial activities, including bank account operations. This provision is
designed to enhance tax compliance, reduce revenue leakage, and improve the integrity of
Nigeria's taxpayer database.
Implementation Date
The mandatory TIN requirement for banking transactions takes full effect on January 1, 2026,
coinciding with the commencement of the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025 and the Nigeria Tax Administration
Act, 2025.
Banks and other financial institutions have been directed to integrate TIN verification into their
account opening and maintenance processes by this date. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and
the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) are coordinating to ensure seamless implementation.

WHAT THE POLICY REQUIRES
For New Bank Accounts
Beginning January 1, 2026, all taxable individuals and entities seeking to open new bank accounts
in Nigeria must provide a valid Tax Identification Number (TIN) as part of the Know Your Customer
(KYC) requirements.
Banks will be required to verify the TIN against the national taxpayer database before approving
new account applications. Failure to provide a valid TIN may result in the bank declining the
account opening request.
For Existing Bank Accounts
Contrary to widespread misinformation circulated in late December 2025, existing bank account
holders will NOT have their accounts blocked or frozen if they do not have a TIN on January 1,
2026.
The Federal Inland Revenue Service (now NRS) has clarified that account holders without a TIN
will be asked to supply it 'as time goes on' through a gradual, customer-friendly process. Banks will
engage existing customers to update their records, but no punitive measures such as account
freezing or restriction will be imposed immediately.
Account holders are, however, encouraged to proactively obtain and link their TIN to avoid potential
compliance issues in future transactions such as large transfers, loan applications, or opening
additional accounts.
CRITICAL CLARIFICATION: NO SEPARATE TIN
REQUIRED
One of the most important clarifications issued by the NRS in December 2025 is that Nigerians do
not need to obtain a separate Tax Identification Number (TIN) to open or operate bank
accounts.
How the System Works
Nigeria's tax administration system has been designed to integrate seamlessly with existing
national identification infrastructure. Specifically:
• For Individuals: Your National Identification Number (NIN) issued by the National Identity
Management Commission (NIMC) serves as your TIN. When you provide your NIN to the bank, it is
automatically linked to the tax system behind the scenes.
• For Companies and Businesses: Your Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) Registration
Number (RC Number) serves as your TIN. Upon registration with CAC, your RC Number is
automatically recognized as your TIN in the NRS database.
• For Other Entities: Trusts, estates, clubs, and other taxable entities registered with CAC or other
regulatory bodies will similarly have their registration numbers integrated into the TIN system.
This integration eliminates the need for individuals and businesses to make separate applications
for TIN. The system operates in the background, ensuring that taxpayer identification is seamless

pages.text:
WHO IS EXEMPT FROM TIN REQUIREMENT?
The TIN requirement applies only to taxable persons—that is, individuals and entities who are
liable to pay tax under Nigerian law. The following categories of persons are exempt and do not
need to provide TIN to open or operate bank accounts:
• Students: Full-time students who do not earn taxable income are exempt from the TIN
requirement. They may open and operate student accounts using their school identification and NIN
without needing a separate TIN linkage.
• Dependents and Minors: Children and dependents (such as those under the age of 18 or those
without independent sources of income) are not required to have TIN to operate bank accounts
opened on their behalf by parents or guardians.
• Non-Income Earners: Individuals who genuinely have no source of income (e.g., the
unemployed, retirees living solely on pensions below the taxable threshold, or persons entirely
dependent on family support) are not required to link TIN to their accounts.
• Religious and Charitable Organizations: Registered religious bodies, charities, and non-profit
organizations whose income is derived exclusively from donations and grants (and not from trade
or business activities) may be exempt, subject to confirmation of their tax-exempt status.
It is important to note that exemption from TIN requirement does not mean exemption from
providing identification. All bank account holders must still comply with standard Know Your
Customer (KYC) requirements, including providing valid NIN or other acceptable forms of
identification.
FACT-CHECK: DEBUNKING MISINFORMATION
In the final days of December 2025, numerous false claims circulated on social media and
messaging platforms, causing unnecessary panic among Nigerian bank account holders. Below are
the most common falsehoods, alongside the verified facts:
Claim 1: Your bank account will be blocked from January 1, 2026 if you don't have TIN.
Fact: FALSE. The NRS and CBN have confirmed that existing accounts will NOT be blocked.
Account holders will be asked to provide TIN gradually, but no punitive action will be taken on
January 1, 2026.
Claim 2: You need to visit FIRS/NRS office to apply for a separate TIN before opening a bank
account.
Fact: FALSE. You do not need a separate TIN. Your NIN (for individuals) or RC Number (for
companies) automatically serves as your TIN. No additional application is required.
Claim 3: Students and unemployed persons cannot open bank accounts from January 2026.
Fact: FALSE. Students, dependents, and non-income earners are exempt from the TIN
requirement and can continue to open and operate accounts using their NIN and other standard
KYC documents.
Claim 4: The government will monitor and tax every bank transaction from January 1, 2026.

HOW TO OBTAIN OR VERIFY YOUR TIN
For Individuals
If you already have a National Identification Number (NIN), you automatically have a TIN. There is
no separate application process. To verify your TIN:
1. Visit the NRS online portal at www.nrs.gov.ng (or successor domain as announced).
2. Navigate to the 'TIN Verification' section.
3. Enter your NIN and personal details (name, date of birth).
4. The system will display your TIN, which is typically identical to or directly derived from your NIN.
5. If you encounter any discrepancies, contact the NRS helpdesk or visit your nearest tax office for
assistance.
If you do not yet have a NIN, you should visit a NIMC enrollment center to register. Once you
receive your NIN, it will automatically serve as your TIN for tax purposes.
For Businesses and Companies
Companies registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) automatically receive a TIN
upon registration. Your CAC RC Number is your TIN.
1. Locate your Certificate of Incorporation or Business Name Registration Certificate issued by
CAC.
2. Your RC Number (Company Registration Number or Business Name Registration Number) is
your TIN.
3. Provide this number to your bank when opening a corporate account.
4. For verification or if you need a formal TIN certificate, visit the NRS online portal or your nearest
tax office.
For Special Cases
Trusts, estates, partnerships, unincorporated associations, and other entities should contact the
NRS directly for guidance on TIN registration. The NRS has established dedicated help desks and
online support channels to assist these categories.
